name: Scotch Game
summary: Open the centre on move 3 and play with active pieces. More forcing than the Italian, with a few lines worth knowing by heart.

notes.5: d4 at once: Black must take, and the open centre favours the side with the lead in development.
notes.9: Be3 defends d4 and asks the bishop on c5 what it is doing; 5...Qf6 keeps the pressure on d4.
notes.11: c3 bolsters d4 and prepares Bc4 or Be2 and f4 later.
notes.17: Castled with a solid centre. The f-pawn goes to f3 (not f4 yet) to keep e4 and stop ...Ng4 ideas.
notes.19: f3: the structure is safe; plans are Kh1, f4 to kick the knight, and pressure on the d-file.

notes.9: Nxc6 and e5 is the whole point: the knight is chased and Black's pawns are doubled on the c-file.
notes.13: Qe2 covers e5 and keeps the queens on; Black's queen on e7 is awkwardly placed in front of the bishop.
notes.15: c4 hits the knight; ...Ba6 pins the pawn for a moment, which b3 solves.
notes.19: f4 cements e5. White's plan is Bb2, Nd2-f3 and queenside play; Black's king is often slow to find a home.

notes.9: Nc3 develops and lets the e-pawn go: the queen on e4 will be hit with tempo.
notes.13: Ndb5 threatens Nxc7+; Black has to give the bishop and move the king.
notes.17: O-O: White is a pawn down but far ahead in development and Black's king sits on d8. Play Ba3, Re1 and Qd2 with the initiative.
